hints.en: `agg(["count", "mean", "std"])` gives all three columns at once.
Apply `.round(2)` to the table and store it in a variable.
The name of the smallest group is `table["count"].idxmin()`.

hints.tr:
Çözüm:

```python
tablo = data.groupby("city")["score"].agg(["count", "mean", "std"]).round(2)

print(tablo)
print(round(data["score"].mean(), 2), data["score"].median())
print(tablo["count"].idxmin())
```
hints.en:
The solution:

```python
table = data.groupby("city")["score"].agg(["count", "mean", "std"]).round(2)

print(table)
print(round(data["score"].mean(), 2), data["score"].median())
print(table["count"].idxmin())
```
